posts.notes: Scheduled automation (/orl-publish --fire) failed to actually fire on 09-08: found two bugs, (1) both scheduled tasks pointed at bare 'claude' which Task Scheduler couldn't resolve -- fixed, (2) the standalone claude.exe CLI's OAuth login had expired -- fixed with an API key. Published manually instead, roughly 11 hours after the intended 00:00 slot. DO NOT mark 00:00 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json based on this entry -- the actual post time diverged too far from the assigned slot to say anything about how 00:00 itself performs. posts.notes: Scheduled ORL-Fire ran at 00:30 (Task Scheduler exit 0) but did nothing -- root cause was a stale OAuth credential file (~/.claude/.credentials.json) blocking claude.exe from ever falling back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in headless mode, compounded by insufficient API balance underneath that. Both fixed (credential file renamed to .bak, balance topped up). Fired manually via /orl-publish --fire run directly in an interactive session instead of retrying the scheduled task, roughly 21.5 hours after the intended 00:30 slot -- DO NOT mark 00:30 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json based on this entry, same reasoning as the 09-08 entry (actual post time too far from assigned slot). linkedin-bot.py --post again exited 1 on the 'Post successful' toast check (same known false-negative as the 09-11 case-study post) but a direct Playwright read of the published-posts page confirmed the post is live with matching text, timestamped 'now' at post time.

posts.notes: Catch-up cycle after the 2-day API-credit outage (09-13/09-14) -- fired manually, ahead of the planned 19:30 slot, right after the user asked to post immediately rather than wait. linkedin-bot.py --post failed twice in a row this time (not the usual toast false-negative -- confirmed via the Browser pane that neither attempt actually posted anything). DO NOT mark 19:30 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json -- actual post time diverged from the planned slot (fired early by request), same reasoning as prior manual-catch-up entries.

posts.notes: Fired manually by direct user request ('Limit is gone. Lets manually publish something today shall we?') rather than waiting for the assigned 19:45 slot to arrive via the automated cycle -- blog built, deployed, and confirmed live (200 OK) before posting. linkedin-bot.py --post exited 1 on the usual toast false-negative; the Browser pane's own LinkedIn session unexpectedly showed a login wall when attempting the normal admin-page verification (first time this specific failure mode has occurred this session -- likely that browser context's cookies expired independently of linkedin-bot.py's own separate persistent profile).
